facts.fact_text: At around 2.20 p.m. on 29 June 2006, the applicants began a demonstration outside the Tbilisi Court of Appeal.
The purpose of the applicants' demonstration on 29 June 2006 was to express their support for Mr Shalva Ramishvili and Mr Davit Kokhreidze.
According to the applicants, the court bailiffs restrained the applicants by force allegedly without prior warning or explanation.
The applicants were taken into the court-house after being restrained by the bailiffs.
The applicants were locked in the bailiffs' duty room of the court-house.
After being confined in the duty room, the applicants were transferred by the police to an Interior Ministry remand centre.
The President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, Mrs E.T., decided to detain the applicants for thirty days on the basis of the bailiffs' written submissions alone.
The period of the applicants' detention expired and they were released on 28 July 2006.
The arrest records stated that the applicants had been arrested on the basis of section 76(3) § 1 (f) of the Courts of Common Jurisdiction Act of 13 June 1997.
The detention of the applicants was ordered under Article 208 § 6(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Article 208 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on the basis of which the applicants were sanctioned by the decision of 29 June 2006, was titled "Liability for breach of public order in court".

Article 208 § 6(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provided that in the event of a breach of public order or contempt committed inside the court building, the President of the court shall be entitled to apply the measures envisaged by Article 208 against the offender.

In its judgment of 15 December 2006, the Constitutional Court criticised the definition of the offence of contempt of court as contained in paragraph 6 of Article 208 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as vague.

The Constitutional Court stated in its judgment of 15 December 2006 that "the offence prescribed by the disputed provision is not clearly formulated... and the interpretation may be ambiguous due to the lack of specificity and vagueness of the provision".

The Constitutional Court stated in its judgment of 15 December 2006 that where legislation introduces a sanction such as detention, an offender must clearly understand the nature of the offence for which he is subjected to detention, and the judge applying the law should be able to do so correctly and adequately.

The arrest records stated that the offenders had "breached public order" in the form of "contempt of court, insults, disregard of the bailiffs' lawful orders to stop the wrongdoing, resistance to the bailiffs, attempts to influence the court by actions and verbal expressions, impeding the administration of justice, and so on".

The President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, Mrs E.T., concluded in the decision of 29 June 2006 that the applicants had "breached public order, shown manifest and gross contempt towards the court and endangered the administration of justice".

Judge Z.M. stated in the decision of 26 July 2006 that the President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal had no other choice but to sanction the applicants under Article 208 § 6(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, since what was at stake was "not the judge's own interests but the authority of the court and the proper administration of justice".
At around 2.20 p.m. on 29 June 2006, the applicants began a demonstration outside the Tbilisi Court of Appeal.
According to the applicants' written statements of 4 and 5 July 2006, the applicants entered the yard of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal through the main gates.
According to the applicants' written statements of 4 and 5 July 2006, the applicants stopped ten to twenty metres from the court-house.
According to the applicants' written statements of 4 and 5 July 2006, the first applicant used a megaphone to utter slogans.
The first applicant uttered the slogan: "We should not have political prisoners in Georgia!"
The first applicant uttered the slogan: "We urge you to obey justice and not the private interests of a number of high officials!"
The first applicant uttered the slogan: "Give me justice or give me death!"
According to the applicants, nothing was displayed or addressed to the court which could be construed as contempt during the incident of 29 June 2006.
The President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, Mrs E.T., decided to detain the applicants for thirty days on the basis of the bailiffs' written submissions alone.

The decision of 29 June 2006 noted the bailiffs' version of the incident, namely that the applicants, "who were inside the court building, in its central entrance, were breaching public order, obstructing the normal functioning of the court and seeking to influence the court with respect to proceedings in a particular case".

The President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, Mrs E.T., concluded in the decision of 29 June 2006 that the applicants had "breached public order, shown manifest and gross contempt towards the court and endangered the administration of justice".
Judge Z.M. stated in the decision of 26 July 2006 that the thirty days' detention had been an appropriate punishment, given the gravity of the acts committed.

At the press conference, the President of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, Mrs E.T., stated: "... five individuals, ... who have shown such direct and gross contempt towards the court and breached public order in the court... I will impose upon them, by my ruling, a form of detention for thirty days, and this will be another good example [of the fact] that respect towards courts and the maintenance of public order in court will be protected very strictly."
